newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD gold find holds 500 tonnes-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD gold find holds 500 tonnes-paper.

text.p: Geologists and advisors to Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) say a new gold deposit in northern Brazil discovered in October holds 500 tonnes, a newspaper said.

CVRD consultant Roberto Assad who visited the Carajas region in Para state in October confirmed the new find will more than double CVRD's gold reserves of currently 450 tonnes to 950 tonnes worth 12 billion reais ($11.54 billion), Folha de Sao Paulo said.

The new gold find places CVRD, which is due to be privatized in April this year, among the largest producers of gold in the world and could increase the company's sell-off price, Folha de Sao Paulo said.
Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND) is meeting February 5 to discuss CVRD's privatization and set the minimum price for the initial sell-off of a 45-percent stake in the company.

CVRD has maintained it is too early to determine the size of the gold deposit and it will take at least another three months of survey work before the size and viability of the deposit can be established with any relative certainty.
--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
